Kia Orana! I’m Nikau from New Zealand. I’m
working at a whale research center in the Cook
Islands. I think humpback whales are the most
amazing animals in the ocean. I have kept a diary
about them ⓐto record my work and thoughts.
July 1st
Finally, the humpback whales are back! They have
traveled about 6,500 km from the Southern Ocean
to give birth. The big and friendly giants came
close to our boat and played for a while. All of a
sudden, they jumped up high and made huge
splashes. Watching whales never ⓑgets boring.
July 17th
Today, I flew a drone to tag humpback whales. I
followed them closely and dropped tags carefully
onto their backs. We get a lot of information about
them from the tags. I am particularly interested in
their songs, and the tags ⓒhave recorded them for
several years. Their songs last up to 30 minutes
and can travel thousands of kilometers underwater!
The songs are beautiful, but we still don’t know
much about them.
August 2nd
I was filming some humpback whales underwater.
Suddenly, one whale came close and pushed me
hard. I tried to swim away, but it kept pushing me
out of the water. I was so surprised. Then
somebody shouted from the boat, “A tiger shark is
coming!” I safely got on the boat. I realized ⓓthat
the whale was trying to save me. Humpback whales
sometimes help other sea animals, but I never
expected them to save my life.
August 5th
This morning, I found a dead humpback whale on
the coast. There were so many plastic bags and
fishing nets in its stomach. Human activities are the
greatest danger to whales. The ocean is home to
whales and other sea animals. I want humans and
sea animals ⓔto live in harmony.
